extracted.intended_audience: prospective NIH grant applicants (investigators, PD/PIs, institutional sponsored programs staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing the narrative sections and attachments of NIH grant applications (Research Plan, Program Plan, budgets, biosketches, resource-sharing plans, letters, and ancillary forms). Targets content, organization, and compliance expectations across common NIH application components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the How to Apply – Application Guide and funding opportunity notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The How to Apply – Application Guide and the funding opportunity are your key references for attachment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm which forms and attachments are required for your particular project by checking both sources. The page advises that your funding opportunity and project may only require a subset of the forms and attachments described here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Research Plan vs Research Training Program Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A Research Plan includes Specific Aims and a Research Strategy; a Research Training Program Plan includes a Program Plan and does not include Specific Aims or a Research Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many attachments are common to both types; always check the funding opportunity and How to Apply – Application Guide to confirm which you must prepare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to Application (resubmissions/revisions only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write an Introduction to Application attachment for resubmission applications, revision applications, or if the funding opportunity specifies one. An introduction is not allowed for new or renewal applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find guidance and requirements specifically in the Resubmission Applications and Competing Revisions instructions about what information to include in the introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: clear, concise, hypothesis-based, one page
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft Specific Aims to encapsulate your specific hypothesis-based goals and expected outcomes; the attachment is limited to one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus Aims on project goals, anticipated outcomes, and resulting overall impact rather than merely describing experiments. Ask mentors/colleagues to review early. Typical R01 proposes ~three related Specific Aims for a 4–5 year grant. Plan Aims achievable within the award timeframe and such that null results still contribute to the field when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy: required structure (Significance, Innovation, Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the Research Strategy with three main sections (in this order): Significance, Innovation, Approach. Include Preliminary Studies (new applications) or a Progress Report (renewals/revisions) either as a subsection of Approach or integrated and clearly labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may address Significance, Innovation, and Approach for each Specific Aim individually or collectively. Use an outline, subheaders, bold running heads, or numbering to enhance readability and help peer reviewers follow the structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy content: describe project, rigor, reproducibility, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the proposed project, its significance, and how you will conduct the research, including principles of scientific rigor, reproducibility, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include necessary detail so reviewers (not all specialists) can evaluate your work. Consider tables, charts, and figures to summarize data and show experimental flow. Do not duplicate Human Subjects/Clinical Trials information already provided on the PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trial Information form. If including images, provide brief descriptions; do not embed/link videos in the Research Strategy (instead follow Video instructions and include a Cover Letter explaining intent to submit a video). Track related information such as budget implications and bibliographic references while drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Research Strategy accessible to non-specialist reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Only some peer reviewers will be familiar with specialized field techniques; the Research Strategy must be clear enough to convince all reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explanatory text, overviews, and clear organization. Consider including an overview outline to help reviewers and avoid excessive jargon or unexplained acronyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Plan (training grants): coherent curriculum and fit
rubrics_metrics.description: For training grants, design a Program Plan that offers a coherent, cogent learning curriculum and training experiences appropriate to the trainee level and that fits the funding opportunity goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize program strengths and advantages for trainees, mentors' commitment and relevant teaching skills, plans for recruiting a diverse trainee pool and matching trainees to mentors, and the organization's commitment to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects, clinical trials, animals, stem cells, select agents: include required additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: If your project involves human subjects, clinical trials, vertebrate animals, human stem cells, or select agents, you must include additional related information and follow specific NIH pages and forms for each area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NIH Human Subjects Research, Clinical Trial Requirements, Guidelines for Human Stem Cell Research, OLAW Vertebrate Animals Section, and Select Agent Information. Some information is requested Just-in-Time (before award) rather than in the initial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan and team attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: If using multiple PD/PIs or consortium/contractual arrangements, finalize agreements and include a Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan and other team attachments as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a strong scientific rationale for multiple PD/PIs, describe the leadership team's organizational structure and conflict resolution procedures, explain how PD/PIs will share data, collaborate on publications, and allocate resources. Include Letters of Support once agreements are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/Contractual Arrangements: costs and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: When another organization will execute a significant proportion of project activities, provide a Consortium/Contractual Arrangements attachment that includes associated costs or rates and a solid explanation of why your organization should be the grant recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about roles, responsibilities, and financial terms for collaborators and contractors, and ensure consistency with statements elsewhere in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support vs Reference Letters: inclusion rules and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of Support (from team members, consortium partners, contractors) are typically included in the application; Reference Letters (for fellowships and some awards) must be provided directly to NIH by referees and not included in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that letters of support detail roles/commitments and any rates/prices for contracted services, and that letter content aligns with statements in the Research Strategy and Budget. Follow the Reference Letters page and funding opportunity-specific instructions for referee submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Letter: optional but required in specified scenarios; limited access
rubrics_metrics.description: A Cover Letter is typically optional and only accessible to NIH staff with a need to know. You must include a cover letter when specified (e.g., late application, intent to submit a video).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funding opportunity special instructions for cover letters and refer to NIH podcast guidance on appropriate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Assignment Request Form: optional assignment suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional form to suggest NIH institute/center/office assignment, study section assignment, use of ART/Matchmaker, and to list potential reviewers with conflicts of interest for exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH DRR staff will consider but may assign differently per referral guidelines. Only NIH staff with a need to know can access this form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans and Data Management & Sharing (DMS) Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine applicable sharing policies and summarize sharing plans (model organisms, research tools, and DMS) in the Resource Sharing Plans and Other Plans attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not providing a plan for material normally required to be shared, include a justification. Find sample DMS plans and recommended elements; you may request funds in the budget to prepare, document, and archive data. Follow NIH Institute/Center-specific data sharing policies and funding opportunity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix policy: very limited allowable materials; non-compliance consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Very few items are allowed in the Appendix. Adding disallowed materials will make the application non-compliant and NIH must withdraw it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Examples of Allowable Appendix Materials, Appendix FAQs, and the NIH podcast on Appendix Policy before adding any appendix items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification: coordination and allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the funding opportunity for required budget type, understand budget components, and work with your Office of Sponsored Research or department administrator to prepare the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact financial/grants management contacts listed in the funding opportunity for questions about allowability. Explain costs related to policies (e.g., Data Management and Sharing) in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketches and SciENcv use; Other Support timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Include eRA Commons credentials and biographical sketches for PD/PIs and all individuals named on the Senior/Key Person Profile Form. Use SciENcv to prepare biosketches. Do not include current and pending (other) support in the application unless the funding opportunity specifies; submit that information Just-in-Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Biosketch Format Pages, Instructions, and Samples. Note that due dates on/after Jan 25, 2026 require new Common Forms prepared using SciENcv for Biographical Sketch, Current and Pending Support, and NIH Biosketch Supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative: audience, content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative will be shared through RePORTER if funded; do not include proprietary/confidential information or descriptions of past accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the Project Summary/Abstract to be informative to others working in the same or related fields and understandable to a science-literate reader. Write the Project Narrative in plain language understandable by a general audience emphasizing the project's public health relevance. See guidance on communicating research intent and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited: scholarly practice and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a bibliography capturing references cited in the Research Plan and other forms. List author names in the same sequence as the publication; you may use “et al.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow scholarly citation practices and do not use hyperlinks unless the funding opportunity specifies. Use NCBI My NCBI to save searches and PubMed citations, and SciENcv to populate Biographical Sketch sections. My Bibliography helps manage NIH Public Access Policy compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources: describe only applicable resources and strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities and resources (laboratory, animal, computer, office, clinical) to be used and their capacities, pertinent capabilities, proximity, and extent of availability to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the scientific environment contributes to the probability of success (institutional support, physical resources, intellectual rapport). Describe only facilities and resources that are directly applicable to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format attachments and page limits: follow stated limits and format rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm page limits and format requirements for attachments and text fields as stated in the funding opportunity and Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Format Attachments, Page Limits, and Rules for Text Fields pages to ensure compliance with form-specific formatting and length constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting practice: track related administrative items while writing
rubrics_metrics.description: While drafting experiments and narrative content, track related budget expenses and bibliographic citations to streamline final assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add full references to the Bibliography & References Cited attachment as you cite them, and note anticipated budget implications to inform the Budget and Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional letters and certifications (other required letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some opportunities require additional letters (e.g., certification of eligibility, institutional letters for training grants describing policies to prevent discriminatory harassment, small business certification letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funding opportunity and How to Apply instructions for any required additional letters and include them where requested or provide them Just-in-Time as indicated.
